    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.
    • It has been revealed that hoYoverse confirmed last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020.
    • The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

    It has been revealed that hoYoverse confirmed last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

    The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

    In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

    Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

    And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's upgrade.

    Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

    It's a bit of a time for AI and games at the moment, 'ey? A bad time, obviously, as it's infecting everything from game development, to the modding community, to native PC ports of a remake of a very popular game that I won't link to for fear of a certain organization finding out where I live and ending me there and then. And of course, the latter may be a concern for one Rockstar Games and the impending release of GTA 6. But according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, game's publisher, they are presently technically and legally preparing themselves.

    It has been revealed that IGN recently spoke to Zelnick regarding potential AI cloning concerns, notably about any business challenges they may face as a result. "I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business," Zelnick explained. "I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.".

    Recent findings suggest that zelnick also made a comment about thinking "all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's," in response to a question about whether he wants to see OpenAI follow in Claude's footsteps by limiting the potential for genAI clones. "If you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected," he mentioned.

    It has been revealed that it was during an investor Q&A where Zelnick dug into the precautions Take-Two are take-twoing in regards to the growing threat of AI. "[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.".

    Essentially: unless you want to face the wrath of the kinds of lawyers multi-billion dollar companies can afford, I wouldn't bother trying to clone GTA 6 with AI! Probably won't end well!

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

    Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

    The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

    According to recent reports, that noted, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

    It has been revealed that the gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet upcoming characters.

    Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

    Sources indicate that beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

    The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

    You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game introduces. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

    Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

    Industry observers note that the Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

    According to recent reports, immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game promptly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

    Sources indicate that these figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

    Industry observers note that like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

    According to recent reports, assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a significant launch.

    Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

    8 Best Ways to Build Lucia and Jason’s Relationship in GTA 6

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1120 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Grand Theft Auto 6 has two main protagonists.
    • Recent findings suggest that they don’t automatically start off being thicker than thieves.
    • Industry observers note that you have to make sure to care about your partner, and not just treat them as any other character in the game.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Grand Theft Auto 6 has two main protagonists. They are Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, and the pair are madly in love with one another. At least, you are going to want them to be. They have a chance to be more like friends by the end of the story.

    Recent findings suggest that they don’t automatically start off being thicker than thieves. Instead, they have a budding relationship that you must help develop, and there are multiple ways that you can help it grow and flourish throughout the game.

    Industry observers note that you have to make sure to care about your partner, and not just treat them as any other character in the game. Do you think you can do that?

    When you start up Grand Theft Auto 6, you play as Jason for a while. You don’t actually start playing as Lucia until the second chapter of the game. This is mostly because the first chapter is dedicated to her getting out of prison and adjusting to life outside.

    Industry observers note that when you get the call that she is getting out of prison soon, you need to start prepping the house if you want her to be happy. This means that you will want to fix the roof, outside steps, and the wall in the bedroom.

    Each of these will help Lucia feel more at home and make her more happy when she gets out of prison, and it will give a serious boost to the relationship.

    Your partner will drop hints in dialogue about things they expect you to do. For instance, Lucia and Jason will go to a bar shortly after she gets out of prison. During this time, she will ask Jason to grab her another drink.

    If you don’t grab her a drink, it will be brought up in the next conversation, and it will ultimately decrease your relationship score because you didn’t listen to what she asked of you.

    You need to pay attention to what your partner says, and if they ask you to do something, it is key that you go out of your way to do it so they don’t get upset.

    Early in the game, you need to set yourself up a BuckMe account. It is this game’s version of Venmo or PayPal, which allows you to send and receive money. It also lets you save money, and that is the key.

    Industry observers note that as part of the story, Lucia and Jason are saving up money for their family. This means that they need to put money aside for the future. This will also help them open a real bank account.

    According to recent reports, whenever you are able to, put money aside so that you can put it towards your future, as this will make your partner very happy. It indicates you are being responsible.

    Recent findings suggest that A big part of any relationship is showing your partner that you care and that you are there for them, and you can do this in multiple ways, but one way is physical affection. This can take many forms, even the simple holding of a hand.

    It has been revealed that whenever Jason and Lucia are together, they have the option to hold hands. You will see the option to hold your partner’s hand in the bottom right corner of the screen. When this appears, it is good to pay attention to it.

    Holding hands in public demonstrates your partner you are there with them and lets them know they can count on you. It’s a simple but important gesture.

    Recent findings suggest that another means of showing your partner that you care is purchasing them gifts. Everyone loves to get a gift, as it indicates that they are being thought about, and the same applies for both Lucia and Jason in GTA 6.

    There are various opportunities for you to purchase gifts for your partner. For instance, Jason can purchase a necklace for Lucia at the start of the game before she gets out of prison.

    Gifts don’t have to be lavish. Instead, you can simply think about what your partner is going to eat. Go out to the store and grab a couple of food items for them and they will definitely be happy about it.

    It should go without saying that your partner should be the one you think of first when doing activities, but it might need to be spelled out for some people. Throughout the game, you have the opportunity to put the needs of your partner first or do other activities.

    If you choose to do something else, they will be upset and you will lose points in your relationship. For instance, there is a time when Lucia will want Jason to talk to Mattia.

    According to recent reports, if you choose to do other things first, like hang out with Cal, Lucia will be noticeably upset with Jason that he chose to do something else before the thing she asked him to do. Putting your partner first will increase your relationship score quickly.

    Sources indicate that after a while, you will have full access to Vice City and the glorious sun-baked land of Leonida. That means that you have plenty of activities you can take part in. At this point in the game, you will be playing the game mostly as a duo, which means you can take part in activities together.

    There are games that can be played like mini-golf, and then there’s other stuff like kayaking that you can do. These are all considered dates, and they are important to take part in, as they will immensely help your relationship.

    As part of the dating mechanic, your partner will mention things they are interested in doing, and taking part in these activities will increase your bond, so make sure you pay attention to what they say while you are out and about.

    Industry observers note that A significant part of GTA 6 is the ability to play as both Jason and Lucia. Rockstar made a big deal about being able to seamlessly switch between these two as you complete missions and explore the world.

    This means that you can take on heists by yourself or you can complete the job with your partner, and it is better overall to do the latter.

    Sources indicate that having your partner with you means that you have twice the manpower, and it also means that you can get more loot, and someone watching your back for if trouble comes. Plus, it raises your relationship status to have your partner in crime by your side.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, you know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

    Sources indicate that this comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony said that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring newly introduced creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

    Bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.".

    It has been revealed that sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

    Recent findings suggest that for those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was announced back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a latest name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

    • Knowing how to get a jet in GTA 6 is essential information if you're planning to cause chaos, as taking control of one of these military aircraft is considered peak criminal behavior.
    • The location for a number of GTA 6 jets is the Mile Zero Air Station, which is found by heading west along the main road from the starting area, through Abismo Key, then on to Southwind and the military base itself.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Knowing how to get a jet in GTA 6 is essential information if you're planning to cause chaos, as taking control of one of these military aircraft is considered peak criminal behavior. While you'd expect that significant progress in GTA 6 would be required before you even had a chance of swiping such high-end hardware, you can actually go and help yourself to one pretty much as soon as you start the game. To try it yourself, here's how to steal a jet in GTA 6.

    The location for a number of GTA 6 jets is the Mile Zero Air Station, which is found by heading west along the main road from the starting area, through Abismo Key, then on to Southwind and the military base itself.

    Sources indicate that you can drive there in any vehicle, though I recommend not using your GTA 6 personal vehicle as it will get trashed and left inside the base, so steal a sturdy and reasonably fast vehicle for the job. Purchasing and equipping body armor from Ammu-nation will also improve your odds of surviving the initial stage.

    Recent findings suggest that follow the route marked on my map above, which will lead you through some barriers on the road to a set of soldiers who will open fire, then take the first turning right and drive through more soldiers until you see a dirt pile ahead that you can hit to clear the security fences. This is also a Stunt Jump, though you don't need to complete it as long as you clear the perimeter and land on the runway.

    It has been revealed that once on the runway inside the miliary base, drive straight ahead to where you'll see several GTA 6 jets parked up next to hangars. Pull up alongside one, jump out of your car and hop straight into the cockpit, before firing up the afterburner and turning onto the runway to take off.

    It has been revealed that once you've taken control of your jet and got airborne, follow the prompt to retract the landing gear and you're away! Be aware that you'll have attracted at least a five-star GTA 6 Wanted Level with this theft, which could go up to six if you start blowing things up, so multiple military jets will be scrambled to shoot you down with homing missiles. I was barely able to reach the first bridge before getting blown out of the sky, but if you fly low and take evasive action you may fare better – good luck!

    If you're looking for an impressive ride that's easier to obtain then here's how to steal the GTA 6 Paul Walker car, which you can then use to arrive in style at the various GTA 6 Strip Club locations around Leonida.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two latest destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

    The two fresh features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

    Recent findings suggest that the Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

    Created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature debuts, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

    It has been revealed that alongside this, the game is also introducing a new virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

    It has been revealed that it is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

    Industry observers note that in order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, planes are, without a doubt, the fastest way to get around the map in GTA VI. They can help you explore areas to find points of interest or simply get to a pinged location in a flash.

    However, finding a plane is easier mentioned than done. In GTA VI, planes are typically found in very specific locations such as airports and airstrips.

    According to recent reports, if you are looking for a sweet plane to take up into the skies, you have come to the right place. Here are the best places to get a plane in Grand Theft Auto VI.

    Players can find an airstrip on the southeast side of the Grassrivers in Mariana County. This airstrip has a plane that’s easy to control, and there is usually no one around, making it easy to steal.

    In the northern section of Belville in Leonard County, you will find Lake Leonida. Next to one of the docks on the lake, you will find a plane that’s easy to steal because the open water acts as a runway and there aren’t many people around.

    In Borrachero Sound, a very small area on the west side of Kelly County, you will find an airstrip that lies next to the water. You'll usually find more than one plane here, so you’ll have options to choose from.

    Recent findings suggest that in the Waning Sands region of Leonard County, you will find an airstrip just outside of Belville. Similar to the plane spot mentioned earlier, you will also find more than one plane at this airstrip.

    Last, but certainly not least, one of the best places to find a plane is, of course, the Vice City International Airport. Known as VCIA, you can find this airport in the southwest section of Vice Dale County.

    In a recent development, keep in mind that VCIA has high security, so stealing a plane can be tricky. However, it is an airport, so it has the most planes available, making it one of the best places to find one.

    In a recent development, if you’d like to get a plane in a more natural way, that doesn’t involve stealing, you can find one during the McKittrick Farm side quest. To start this quest, examine the poster inside the Starlet Motel office (mandatory location in Chapter 2), and the location of the farm will be marked on your map.

    In a recent development, since you’ll be stealing the planes mentioned in this guide, it’s wise to learn how to avoid the cops when flying. Even though the places I mentioned here tend to have almost no one around, with the exception of VCIA, there’s still a possibility that someone will spot you stealing it or report the crime once they realize it's missing.

    The best way to avoid cops' detection when flying a plane is to fly at low altitude. Flying low makes it harder for cops to see you, as buildings, trees, and other structures will help block their line of sight.

    It has been revealed that you only really need to worry about this if the heat star level reaches 3 to 4, when police bring in the helicopters. Otherwise, you can easily lose cops by simply flying away due to how fast planes go in the game.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the Grand Theft Auto games have always been synonymous with America; Americana is baked into the crime series' very being. Across its history, there's only ever been one GTA game set outside America: the London-based expansion of the original game.

    Sources indicate that GTA 6 follows this template, parodying the American state of Florida and the city of Miami. But what about the next game - will the series always be in America? Not necessarily.

    In an interview with The Guardian, Rockstar North co-studio boss Rob Nelson propped the proverbial door open a sliver by saying: "Never say never." He then quickly followed that comment with: "But there’s still so much to do in America".

    Industry observers note that this is a topic Rockstar has responded to before, most notably when organization co-founder and long-time GTA writer Dan Houser - who's no longer at Rockstar - discussed why the series always seemed to return to America. He said it was because cities like Miami and Latest York and Los Angeles are places where extreme juxtapositions exist. They're places where extreme wealth rubs shoulders with extreme poverty, and where organised crime can be found.

    There's also something America infamously has that few other countries do, and that's free availability of guns, which is such a core tenet of a GTA experience.

    Nevertheless, Obbe Vermeij - a former technical director at Rockstar North - revealed last year that a GTA: Tokyo almost happened. However, it wasn't going to be made by Rockstar but rather an external team in Japan.

    In a recent development, while discussing the subject, Vermeij referred to America as "basically the epicenter of Western culture". "Everybody knows the cities, even people who haven't been there," Vermeij stated. "They have a mental image of the cities. I'm afraid we're stuck in this loop of about five American cities. Let's just get used to it.".

    GTA 6 is just days away from its 19th November release on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar recently clarified the game runs at 30FPS across all platforms and confirmed that while it's available through Xbox Cloud Gaming, it cannot be streamed to PCs or non-Xbox devices.

    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Pcgamer ↗ Open Full Page

    PC gamers notice Nvidia's drivers hammering their SSDs with tens of GB/hr of unnecessary writes – revert to 621.01 ASAP

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (557 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Another day, another dodgy driver: Nvidia's latest driver package (621.24) is needlessly writing to consumers' SSDs, in some cases by 30 GB every hour.
    • The concern appears to be fairly widespread going from reports on the Nvidia GeForce forum, Dell forum, Super User forum, and many, many threads on Reddit.
    • You can then see how much each process has written, which shouldn't usually be very much at all.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Another day, another dodgy driver: Nvidia's latest driver package (621.24) is needlessly writing to consumers' SSDs, in some cases by 30 GB every hour. And if that sounds familiar, it's because an issue with Radeon Adrenalin drivers did a similar thing a week ago.

    The concern appears to be fairly widespread going from reports on the Nvidia GeForce forum, Dell forum, Super User forum, and many, many threads on Reddit. Though that's a bunch of people that might, and did, notice random writes to their SSD; many more may not visit their task manager to check these things with any regularity.

    You can then see how much each process has written, which shouldn't usually be very much at all. I measured my own PC on an older driver version (621.01) and this process had only written 63 MB in an hour of uptime; if you're on the most recent GeForce driver package (621.24), and NVDisplay.Container.exe has a number of gigabytes next to it (it's in bytes, so get your calculator out), you've been bit by the bug.

    The affected driver, 621.24, is still available to download right now. That's the surprising thing here, as the issue has seemingly been reported across the internet since November 15; the driver was released on November 12, and it appears to have taken a few days of needlessly huge writes for anyone to notice.

    The culprit appears to be a binary log stored at 'C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\nvtopps\nct\nvlog.nvlgstg'.

    This log is being constantly rewritten, rather than appended to, according to the initial report by TroubleGrid. The large file is rewritten each time, therefore it keeps growing over a short period while a PC is switched on; the problem with multiplication like that is repeated multiplication leads to exponential growth. If those writes are sustained around the 1–2 MB/s mark, that's upwards of 5–7 GB/hr, though some people suggest it gets much worse.

    The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products.

    It has been revealed that the easiest fix is to revert to the previous driver, 621.01 (clean install option on Nvidia installer or use Display Driver Uninstaller first). There is another fix for anyone hoping to keep the latest Game Ready support, as posted by one user on Reddit and generated by Claude. That's a command that changes the Registry to prevent further writes, while retaining functionality of other Game Ready driver features.

    What's most surprising here is that the driver is still live on Nvidia's site—it should've been pulled days ago.

    #74981. Breaking: Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO states – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

    Breaking: Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO states – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

    📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1071 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that in the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio.
    • Without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone.
    • Dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that in the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Manufacturer of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.

    Without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Manufacturer of Heroes provides.

    Dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013. This was in the immediate aftermath of publisher THQ's bankruptcy auction, where studios and franchises were sold off to the highest bidder. While Sega bought the studio, they didn't buy the licenses to everything Relic had created. "The other games that Relic made – Homeworld, Impossible Creatures, The Outfit... formative games in many people's memory – they were all split up, scattered," Dowdeswell states. "I think that was... I won't say a tragedy, but it's unfortunate because Relic is the home of those games. It would have been great for them to stay with the studio.".

    It has been revealed that just as a hint of the messy history of acquisitions and auctions: this year we see Dawn of War 4 coming from studio King Art Games and published by Deep Silver. Deep Silver are a subdivision of Plaion, formerly called Koch Media, which was acquired by Embracer Group back when they were called THQ Nordic. Not that they were actually the THQ that originally published Relic's Dawn of War, Nordic Games renamed themselves THQ Nordic after they bought the THQ trademark at auction.

    In a recent development, as for Homeworld, Borderlands developer Gearbox picked up the license to the sci-fi RTS in the bankruptcy auction, then contracted Blackbird Interactive's support on the remasters, before handing the latter lead development on Homeworld 3. That chain of events does have a more clear throughline to Relic's past however, as Blackbird was created by two of Relic's co-founders Rob Cunningham and Jon Aaron Kambeitz. (Speaking of studios struggling without the series they made their name with, Blackbird was on the verge of bankruptcy before Gearbox got in touch with the Homeworld work. So we very nearly existed in a world where they never got to make the brilliant Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak and Hardspace Shipbreaker.).

    Anyway, this is all getting side-tracked. Back to holding onto Organization of Heroes when separating from Sega. "Fighting for Company of Heroes when leaving Sega was crucial because I already lamented the fact that the other games didn't come with Relic," Dowdeswell states. "I couldn't really imagine a Relic where none of the games that the studio has made and was known for were any longer part of it.".

    It has been revealed that relic and fresh owner UK investment firm Emona Capital LLP were able to negotiate Firm of Heroes as part of the sale from Sega and since then the studio has spent the past two years focusing largely on supporting the WW2 RTS and restoring their back catalogue. The most recent update is the massive 3.0 patch to mark the series' 20th anniversary. Which, among many changes, overhauls the Mediterranean-set RTS game's special effects, audio systems, NPC AI, and makes significant changes to the singleplayer grand strategy-inspired Italy campaign, as well as adding a whole set of autumn and winter-themed assets for community map makers. They've also released a series of DLCs adding new factions to Company of Heroes 3's skirmishes and multiplayer, re-released Dawn of War with a definitive edition and announced they're doing the same for the original Company of Heroes, along with Blackbird Interactive's help. Dowdeswell notes foundation building masks a lot of the work going on behind the scenes: "We now self-publish all of this," he explains. "There were a number of things that we had to learn, skills we had to develop, capacity and capability that we had to build at the studio very, very promptly.".

    Sources indicate that I ask if it was always the proposal to focus on their back catalogue, or if they had plans to release new games. Dowdeswell claims spending four years quietly working on a new game wasn't an option: "It's almost impossible to do it that way because of the current climate in the industry. We don't have a financial safety net." Though, the team do have larger ambitions. "We want to make new games, we want to provide a modern Relic game," Dowdeswell says. "That ambition to re-establish Relic as an innovator in this strategy space is a significant part of what drives our creative direction on new games." Focusing on updating Company of Heroes 3, releasing DLC for the game, and making definitive editions of Dawn of War and the original Company of Heroes is what gets the studio to the place it can make a new game.

    However, Dowdeswell resists any framing of Relic's work on Manufacturer of Heroes 3 as spinning their wheels or resting on their laurels while working toward a upcoming game. He argues the game "sits in between" Relic's past and its future: "It's an established game that came out three years ago, but it's also a way for us to take some chances, experiment a little bit, and while doing that staying really closely connected to the players, That's what the idea was behind the updates because it was a way to have very quick iterations and touch points with players and provide, honestly, a way for us to fund everything in the future.".

    Recent findings suggest that as to what Relic is making next, Dowdeswell wouldn't say. Though, he revealed trying genres besides real-time strategy was "almost a certainty", before adding "I don't think it's going to be a vast departure for where we are, so it will still be strategic gameplay. We're not going to go build a racer.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love.
    • As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year.
    • It has been revealed that the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

    As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

    It has been revealed that the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the firm's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be confirmed tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

    Industry observers note that this batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

    In a recent development, last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

    What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

    Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

    📅 06 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (872 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The big Diablo 4 Developer Upgrade has indeed delivered the goods.
    • You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.
    • Industry observers note that season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The big Diablo 4 Developer Upgrade has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

    You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

    Industry observers note that season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

    In a recent development, patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

    Recent findings suggest that when you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

    Recent findings suggest that starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

    If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

    Industry observers note that elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

    In a recent development, the Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

    Industry observers note that anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

    It has been revealed that there are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

    In a recent development, the other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

    It has been revealed that even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

    The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the new class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

    The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

    Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

    Recent findings suggest that the more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

    Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has announced he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the manufacturer.
    • In a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox mentioned Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the firm's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027.
    • "I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester said of his decision.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, paradox Interactive's Frederik Wester has announced he's stepping down from the role of CEO after a combined decade and a half leading the manufacturer. The news follows several tumultuous years for the publisher best known for grand strategy games including Stellaris, Europa Universalis, and Crusader Kings 3.

    In a statement announcing the change in leadership, Paradox mentioned Wester had "decided to step down as CEO to continue focusing on the firm's long-term development as a member of the Board." Paradox's current deputy CEO, Mattias Lilja, will take over Wester's role from 4th January 2027. Wester is to remain in the position until then in order "to ensure an orderly transition".

    "I'm truly grateful to all our engaged players and talented colleagues who contribute to outstanding gaming experiences every day," Wester said of his decision. "They are the ones who made these years amazing. My initiative was never to be CEO for life. The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the organization's journey. Since I returned as CEO, we've streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over. Given his experience and vision, he is exceptionally well positioned to take the company to its next level.".

    It has been revealed that wester has twice served as Paradox CEO since joining the organization in 2003. His first stint ran from 2009 to 2018, after which he became Paradox's executive chairman of the board. He returned to the CEO role in 2021, and has overseen a troubled period for the company. This has included the embattled development of Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2 - which finally launched last October after multiple delays, near cancellation, and a switch in developer. Unfortunately the game failed to resonate with critics and audiences, and Paradox confirmed a 162 percent decline in operating profit earlier this year as a result of its commercial failure.

    In a recent development, wester's most recent watch - which began with an admittance of "inappropriate behaviour" amid a damning report into Paradox's workplace culture - has also seen the high-profile cancellation of Sims competitor Life By You, an indefinite delay for Prison Architect 2 after Paradox parted ways with original developer Double Eleven, and a split with BattleTech studio Harebrained Schemes following the commercial failure of The Lamplighters League. Paradox's Cities Skylines 2 has also been blighted with controversy: after a disastrous launch in 2023, its console release is still yet to emerge, and development is now being handled by a new studio after Paradox split with former developer Colossal Order last year. In 2004, Wester admitted the publisher had "made the wrong calls in several projects".

    Despite all this, incoming CEO Mattias Lilja remains buoyant. "Paradox has a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games," he wrote in a statement announcing his promotion. "Now we’re stepping up the pace: we will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus.".

    Paradox, does of course, have some promising games on its upcoming slate. Alongside continued work on grand strategy stalwarts like Crusader Kings 3, Europa Universalis 5, and Stellaris, next year sees the release of Lego Skylines, and post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld is also on the way.

    #74977. 10 Game Boy Metroidvanias You Can Finish in Under 10 Hours

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1059 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

    10 Game Boy Metroidvanias You Can Finish in Under 10 Hours

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1059 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • For a long time, Metroidvanias have been a bit of an oddball when compared to some other games.
    • Very few games ever even attempted to push the envelope of Metroidvanias aside from those that coined the term, Metroid and Castlevania.
    • Industry observers note that the Game Boy, Game Boy Color, and Game Boy Advance could see players complete the game in one long car ride, provided it wasn’t too dark outside just yet.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    For a long time, Metroidvanias have been a bit of an oddball when compared to some other games. They’re still great games, sometimes the best titles of a console generation, but back in the day they were more niche.

    Very few games ever even attempted to push the envelope of Metroidvanias aside from those that coined the term, Metroid and Castlevania. One of the biggest draws of these games is that you could complete them pretty quickly, especially when it came to the handheld consoles.

    Industry observers note that the Game Boy, Game Boy Color, and Game Boy Advance could see players complete the game in one long car ride, provided it wasn’t too dark outside just yet. This list encompasses the shortest Metroidvanias of the broader Game Boy generation that you could finish in under ten hours.

    It has been revealed that starting off with a strange one that fits a bit more into a Metroidvania-like category, Wario Land 3 did incorporate a lot of aspects of Metroidvanias. Playing as the treasure-obsessed Wario, players would navigate various levels attempting to find all the treasure chests available.

    In a recent development, in true Metroidvania fashion, players could return to older levels of the game with fresh abilities to uncover other secrets they couldn’t get to before. The game did manage to make a name for itself thanks to some innovative gameplay elements and its relatively quick run-through.

    In a recent development, now the Castlevania series is absolutely a true Metroidvania, and one of the more difficult by many people's standards. Playing as Nathan Graves, players will enter Dracula’s Castle in an attempt to rescue their mentor.

    Recent findings suggest that while not part of the main continuity of Castlevania, the game gained a following thanks to the difficulty and use of the Dual Set-Up System. This system gave players the ability to create new combinations of attacks via a card-collecting system, for interesting results.

    Many of the best Castlevania games incorporate some sort of gimmick to make them a bit more interesting, and Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance is no exception. Fifty years before Simon Belmont took on Dracula, there was Juste Belmont and their journey through Dracula’s Castle.

    The main feature of the game was the two versions of Dracula’s Castle that saw players moving between the two to solve mysteries and unlock paths intertwined between them. That’s probably the reason the game is on the longer side compared to most of the other Metroidvanias of the time.

    In a surprising twist, this Castlevania game is actually set in the future, in 2035. It also abandoned the Belmonts for a brand new protagonist, Soma Cruz, who would discover his strange ability after being drawn to the castle during an eclipse.

    In keeping with the lore of the game, the major system here was called the Tactical Soul System, and it would allow Soma to gain new abilities based on the soul he collected. This drove the main idea behind the Metroidvania aspects of the game and granted some freedom in character builds that players enjoyed.

    Whether you’ve heard of the series or seen something from it, almost everyone can recognize Shantae for one reason or another. The series rolled out in 2002 with some great Metroidvania elements that gained a large following, making it fairly popular.

    The game introduced players to the half-genie protagonist Shantae as she did battle against her arch-nemesis Risky Boots. The key feature of the game was that Shantae could dance to transform herself into animals to perform different tasks and movement challenges, accessing other areas.

    The first Metroid game on the list, but not the first to pioneer the series, Metroid Fusion was the fourth game in the series. It brought a different kind of focus to the series, with the game sticking more to narrative and suspense than previous installments.

    This proved to be a great idea as the game revolved around Samus Aran and the infamous SA-X, a duplicate made with an infected suit. It brought an air of suspense to the game that stuck with players despite how short the game was.

    Unlike some of the other Metroid games, Metroid: Zero Mission sought to update the original game for a more modern era. Zero Mission introduced a lot of quality-of-life features to make the age of the original game a bit more manageable.

    Sources indicate that the game took pieces from previous titles that it had learned from, incorporating more story and expanded content. While still short, Metroid: Zero Mission managed to set a newly introduced path for the Metroid series as a whole, and is still seen as one of its highlights.

    It has been revealed that the second game in the series, Metroid II: Return of Samus, is one of the most iconic of all. This title introduced a few of the most memorable features that would become staples of the series, like the Spider Ball.

    Not only did the game introduce some new mechanics, but it also focused on a darker world and story for the Metroidvania. The game clearly helped to build a dedicated fanbase despite its shortness, as its influences can be seen even in the newer Metroid releases today.

    A Metroidvania before the genre was even established, TMNT III: Radical Rescue was arguably one of the first few Metroidvanias. It featured a story focused on rescuing the turtles from the claws of Shredder in a beat-em-up exploration-focused game.

    According to recent reports, each of the four turtles had a special use that would unlock more of the map for you to explore, effectively making the game a great Metroidvania-style game. There’s certainly an argument to be made that it would go on to inspire features in the genre.

    Industry observers note that A controversial title that ended up being basically expelled from the series for narrative reasons. It was a bit different from other entries in the series, being a more stage-based game rather than focusing on traditional navigation.

    It has been revealed that regardless of any of that, the game is the shortest Metroidvania from the Game Boy era, clocking in at around two hours total. While perhaps not the most key Metroidvania over the years, it certainly has its place in history and our hearts. What a little curio.

    #74975. Casualties: Unknown is a total pain simulator that makes other survival games seem like massive cowards

    📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1368 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

    Casualties: Unknown is a total pain simulator that makes other survival games seem like massive cowards

    📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1368 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.
    • You haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics.
    • According to recent reports, I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.

    You haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics. This is an intricate and imaginative celebration of pain - not merely an exacting survival game full of gauges to manage, but a laboratory study of just how many ways an animal body can feel, before it finally gives up the ghost.

    According to recent reports, I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks. I am the sorrowing vat-grown pup of a conclave of star-faring Dr Moreaus. My task is to collect... something, some gadget of great importance, from a cave on a deathly planet, located beneath three kilometres of booby-trapped and infested, poisonous and hateful rock.

    Recent findings suggest that right now, I am trying to burrow into a sealed titanium drop pod with my bare paws, so that I can sleep somewhere warm. Too warm, in fact. The drop pod heaters feel like they were vindictively designed to discourage occupants from lingering, but I'm finding that dehydration is easier to address than hypothermia - there are pools of groundwater around that harbour only a slight risk of "minorly" fouling my intestines. So into the pod we go. After ripping away a layer of rubber, I smash some glass panes and promptly step in the fragments.

    My computer screams, a hideous jangle of chords and static. The interface becomes a fritzing, flexing sphincter of pinks and reds. My punctured dogsbody flops and writhes, spurting yellow fluids and gobs of unintelligible text, ignoring my button inputs. They are my avatar no longer. They have been reduced to a squirming facet of the simulation's agony.

    I gawp in guilt and terror at the status bar, now jammed with pulsing icons, then switch to my health display and determine that I am "bleeding catastrophically" from my right hind paw. I need to bandage that paw swiftly. But first, I need to remove the glass. This takes the form of a 'minigame' in which I guide a shaking clawed hand with the cursor, hauling out shards even as my poor character threatens to pass out from the ordeal.

    According to recent reports, I've got two of five shards out when the earthquake kicks in. Already doubled over and delirious, my pioneering pooch is released over the nearest cliff. They fall about 50 feet, rag-dolling off crags with a concussive whump, till they smash into a flooded wooden platform. The anatomical diagram on the health screen lights up like a wickerman. I don't appear to have broken any bones, but everything is hurting. What's more, I am soaking wet and hypothermia is taking hold, stretching blue veins through the clenching colours of my pain. The screen begins to look like some exotic, putrid flower.

    Wringing my hands, I allow my mutant mutt about 10 seconds to recover from the shock of the fall, then open the health screen again and slowly tug out the last three shards of glass. It's actually easier than before, but not for the happiest of reasons: landing on my head appears to have numbed my senses. There will be longer term consequences, probably. Now I just have to bind the wound… except that I must have dropped my roll of gauze, while tumbling through the abyss. With sirens still flashing on the HUD, I peer about for a cave plant or other source of crafting materials. On the other side of the platform, I spy the corpse of another pitiful lab experiment. Perhaps there's a bandage in that huddle of clothes?

    According to recent reports, I hoist my sagging and babbling starpup to their feet, and limp over to investigate. Then I step on a pressure plate, and a six foot blade shoots up through my left thigh.

    The screen is almost obliterated by crimson snow. The noise is... indescribable. I open the health screen again to assess the damage but I can't, because my dogperson has fallen into utter derangement. They want to be rid of their too-fruitful arteries, their stinking yellow blood. The clawed hand reappears, and I am forced to rake my own torso with it to regain access to the controls.

    According to recent reports, I am now gushing my life out from head to foot. Going by my plummeting heart rate, I have about 30 seconds to burn before I lose consciousness forever. I see no means of recovery, and I can't bear to watch my character bleed out. So instead, I detonate the chip embedded in their brain - the same chip responsible for the interface's rash of icons and warnings. According to the subsequent mission report print-out, my canine pioneer was feeling "dejected" when their head exploded.

    Sources indicate that the worst thing about the scenario I've just recalled is that it represents Casualties: Unknown at its least punishing. All of the above took place in the first of the game's 11 biomes - each procedurally generated, and 300 metres high - on the default "Tough" run setting. Resources are more plentiful up here, while active threats are fewer. There is scope to faff about and prepare - gathering plant matter for a crude woven bag, so I don't have to carry everything in my hands or mouth or tuck it into the folds of my body. There is time to crack open supply crates, and craft an implement of some kind.

    Sources indicate that the main danger, traps aside, is falling. Casualties: Unknown's terrain generator is not your pal. As regards the opening couple of biomes, at least, it works like a broken muck spreader, ejecting a mix of filthy clogs and particles that snag your jumps and often oblige you to dig through rock and gravel. You'll frequently be doing that in the dark, and even the smallest of exertions takes a perceptible toll – whimpers of effort, wheezing breath, double vision. The one major consolation is that you can wall-jump and slide down surfaces, a mocking touch of Prince of Persia.

    Industry observers note that still, further down is where life gets truly unpleasant. There are sonic traps in certain biomes that cause brain damage and massive hemorrhaging. There are vast, rumbling insects you simply cannot afford to get close to, because they are guaranteed to bite off a limb. And the absolutely dreadful thing about that is that it won't necessarily end your run: given a tourniquet and antibiotics, you may yet pull through. Perhaps you'll find or craft a prosthetic. The game's characters are, in general, astonishingly tough for all their immense capacity for anguish.

    Casualties: Unknown is a brilliant and unusual piece of design, uninhibited by any commercialised and sanitary notions of 'fun' and 'difficulty'. It's committed to recreating the surge of sensation through flesh. There's something intrinsically vital about this. Like Project Citadel, perhaps, its extravaganzas of torment are about feeling more present and alive in a twisted world, more in control. I'm not the writer to discuss this, and I know little about the developer's circumstances, but it feels like an exploration of trans survival in the face of a brutalising biopolitical regime: the online wiki notes that the game's zoomorphic Experiments or "Expies" have their own ideas about gender, though I'm finding it tricky to distinguish those accounts from the categorisations of the evidently unfriendly boffins who engineered them.

    I would like to get to the bottom of things. I would like to find that goddamn gadget. I would like to return to the surface and massacre the bastards who sent me down here. Still, I'm not sure I have the willpower to witness everything my avatar might have to endure: barotrauma, sepsis, strokes, ruptured ears, hallucinations... As I've hopefully made clear throughout this piece, it remains an open question as to whether I am them, or simply one of their human tormentors. You can read more on Steam and Itch.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • With GTA 6, Rockstar has created a game few other developers could even dream of competing with.
    • According to recent reports, 21% of Rockstar, representing about 1,000 employees, have been at the company for more than 10 years, a spokesperson tells Bloomberg.
    • In a recent development, nintendo offers one of the most notable counter-examples, where the same five developers who worked on the original Super Mario Bros.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    With GTA 6, Rockstar has created a game few other developers could even dream of competing with. That's partly down to the game's lengthy development cycle and massive budget, but you can also thank Rockstar's willingness to keep its veteran employees around when so many other studios are willing to lay off their most experienced developers.

    According to recent reports, 21% of Rockstar, representing about 1,000 employees, have been at the company for more than 10 years, a spokesperson tells Bloomberg. Admittedly, that tenure only covers two major latest releases – Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 6 – but developers with a decade or more of experience at a single studio are becoming a rare breed.

    In a recent development, nintendo offers one of the most notable counter-examples, where the same five developers who worked on the original Super Mario Bros. were still in the credits of Super Mario Bros. Wonder nearly 40 years later. Rockstar hasn't been around for 40 years, but many of the names you'll find in the credits have been there since the PS2 era, when GTA fever had just started to reach its absurd highs.

    Other publishers, meanwhile, are laying off even their most experienced staff by the bucketload. Devs like Fallout's Tim Cain are warning of the consequences of cutting off institutional knowledge even as Microsoft cuts off developers who'd been making megahits like The Elder Scrolls for decades. How can The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel live up to expectations when the people who know how to make Elder Scrolls games are constantly being laid off?

    Clearly, Rockstar has been more willing to hang onto its veteran staff – unless, of course, we're talking about the 34 union-associated employees it fired in 2025. Disputes over those firings and the union itself are still ongoing, and ugly allegations about continued crunch at Rockstar are coming up as a result.

    On top of all that, GTA 6 devs are "worried about getting laid off" even after "working on the biggest game of all time," and it's clear that there's no true insulation from the threat of layoffs when an executive decides your name is on the wrong side of a spreadsheet. Those fears remain even as GTA 6 itself stands as a monolithic example of what a group of experienced developers are truly capable of.

    Grand Theft Auto 6 success isn't enough to stop the layoffs, former Square Enix exec argues, as Rockstar has "built the biggest, most expensive game of all time and now released it".

    Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest major action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.
    • The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.
    • It has been revealed that since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

    The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

    It has been revealed that since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Upgrade to actually see it in action.

    It has been revealed that the Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

    The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

    In a recent development, the Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

    The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

    Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

    According to recent reports, lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Developer FromSoftware has announced that online multiplayer servers for Dark Souls 2 and 3 are back online following a nearly two-week outage.

    Recent findings suggest that fromSoftware temporarily disabled multiplayer on 30th October, citing what it called "a server concern". Some speculated this could be related to the recently discovered PHP security bug, which impacted a number of other games.

    According to recent reports, fromSoftware never specified the exact problem impacting its servers, and today's statement is equally vague. "Regarding the temporary suspension of the game server for Dark Souls 2, and Dark Souls 3, the investigation has been completed and the fix has been applied. The game server and online features are now restored," a notice on Dark Souls' official site reads.

    "We sincerely apologise for the inconvenience caused, and thank you for your patience and understanding.".

    Online servers do more in FromSoftware games than simply facilitating co-op and PvP; they're also responsible for handling messages players leave for each other in-game, as well as the ghostly representations of players who just went through the same area, helping the Dark Souls series' forlorn worlds feel a little less solitary.

    Industry observers note that this isn't the first time Dark Souls servers have gone offline, either. In 2022, servers for all three games went offline due to a vulnerability that allowed malicious code to run on them. In that instance, it took FromSoftware three months to bring servers back online for some games, and as many as nine months for others.

    In other FromSoftware news, the studio recently announced - following months of speculation - it's officially delaying the Switch 2-exclusive The Duskbloods to sometime in 2027.
